unit.why: A single narrative: R. Aharon ha-Levi (of Staroselye) tells his hasidim that the Besht came to him in a dream during Kabbalat Shabbat and asked him to join ten tzaddikim taken to the upper world to annul an evil decree, and he dies immediately after.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי מעשה מהרה״ק הר׳ אהרן הלוי זצ״ל
stories.summary_en: R. Aharon ha-Levi, a disciple of the Tanya's author, prays Kabbalat Shabbat at the prayer stand. At kiddush he tells his hasidim that the Besht appeared to him in a dream and asked him to complete a minyan of ten tzaddikim who would ascend to annul an evil decree on Israel. He agreed, lay down on his bed and died at once.

tags.why: The tale centres on the tzaddik's death.
The story is set on Friday night, Kabbalat Shabbat and kiddush.

quotes: בא הבעש״ט אצלי בחלום מעולם העליון
tags.why: The Besht appears to him in a dream.

quotes: בא הבעש״ט אצלי בחלום מעולם העליון ואמר לי
tags.why: The deceased Besht speaks to him from the upper world.

quotes: שיקחו עשרה צדיקים מעולם הזה לעולם העליון
tags.why: The upper world is the destination of the tzaddikim.

quotes: שהיה מתפלל בשבת קודש לפני העמוד בקבלת שבת
tags.why: He leads the prayer before the prayer stand.
The tzaddikim give their lives to avert a heavenly decree on Israel.

quotes: נגזרה גזרה רעה על בני ישראל
tags.why: The tzaddikim shield the community from the decree.

quotes: ופעל שיקחו עשרה צדיקים מעולם הזה
tags.why: It shows the tzaddikim's power to annul decrees on others' behalf.
Kiddush implies wine, but the drinking itself is not described.

quotes: שהיה תלמידו של הרב בעל התניא

tags.why: His willing self-sacrifice for Israel is implied rather than stated.

missing_concepts: self-sacrifice of tzaddikim to annul a decree (death as atonement)
minyan of ten tzaddikim in heaven
a deceased tzaddik (the Besht) summoning a living one
